chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Abd al-A'ala, the mawla of the family of Sam, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, among the obligatory rights of the Muslim upon his brother is answering his invitation.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on responding to a Muslim's invitation for a meal?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni transmits this chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish that responding to a meal invitation is a mandatory social right (haqq al-muslim), reflecting the communal solidarity emphasized in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining kinship ties (silat al-rahim) and fulfilling social obligations, distinguishing it from mere voluntary courtesy. The hadith serves as a foundational text for the etiquette of dining and community bonding in Shia ethical traditions.
